name: Riot Grrrl

media.title: Bikini Kill, Pussy Whip EP / early 90s releases
Bust and the riot grrrl zine network
media.note: DIY print culture spread the look as much as the music did

reacts_against: mainstream music industry sexism and the male-dominated punk scene it grew out of; the clashing cute/aggressive styling (barrettes plus slurs written on skin) was itself the political statement.
revivals: 2016–present, cited repeatedly in pop-feminist fashion coverage; direct visual quotation in 2020s 'coquette-meets-punk' TikTok trends

wiki_facts.key_motifs: DIY zines and publications; handwritten text and collage; visible protest slogans; reclaimed derogatory terms; unpolished aesthetics
wiki_facts.key_colours: Black, pink, red, white, ivory, dark grey
wiki_facts.key_values: Feminism, anti-consumerism, rejection of the mainstream, DIY ethos, female empowerment, social activism

findings: mostly muted — about 83% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from Aesthetics Wiki photos as photographed and displayed on screen; actual garments and materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
